=== AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Rules for every coding agent in this repo: Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. Short on purpose.

## Context
- `docs/hack/BRIEF.md`: event, prizes, deadlines.
- `docs/SPEC.md`: what we build, the demo path.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: stack, lanes, contracts.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`: decisions so far.

Read only what your issue needs.

## The loop
One issue = one agent = one worktree/branch = one PR. Humans assign issues. Never pick your own.

1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <claude|codex|cursor>`.
2. Context before code: `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"`,
   `entire brain brief "<task>"`. Run `entire why <file>:<line>` before rewriting code you did not write.
3. Build inside the issue's Scope, in small commits.
4. `./hq check` must pass.
5. Open the PR: `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`.
6. Trail: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`, then `entire trail ci-pr`.
7. Unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`, fix the findings,
   `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass`, then `entire trail ready`.
8. Stop and report. Only when a human says "ship it": `./hq ship <PR>`.

Full detail: `.agents/skills/hq-work/SKILL.md`. Also useful: `./hq board`, `./hq setup --check`.
Windows: use `hq.cmd` or `python tools/hq/hq.py` wherever this file says `./hq`.

## Git
- Work only in your own worktree and branch. Never commit on `main` (a hook blocks it).
- Stage files by name. Never `git add -A` or `git add .`.
- Never revert, checkout, stash or delete changes you did not make.
- Never amend or force-push commits that are already pushed.
- Before `./hq pr`, rebase on `origin/main` (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`) and fix
  your own conflicts. If your branch is already pushed, `git merge origin/main` instead.
- Commit and push your own branch freely. No need to ask.

## Coordination
- GitHub is the only shared state. `.context/` is your private scratch.
- Out-of-scope work becomes a new issue (`gh issue create`), not a drive-by edit.
- Never edit paths listed under "Do not touch" in your issue.
- Progress notes go in issue comments: `gh issue comment N --body "..."`.
- Stuck: `./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.
- Contract changes (shared types, API shapes) need their own issue.

## Definition of done
- Every acceptance criterion is met.
- `./hq check` passes, with its tail in the PR body.
- The PR is open with evidence: what you ran and what you saw.
- Review passed (`review:pass`), unless the issue is `size:S`.

## Issues are approved designs
Do not run brainstorming, spec or plan-document rituals for issue work. Plan inline, then build.

## Entire
Entire records every session and pushes transcripts with your commits.
- Never paste secrets, tokens or `.env` contents into prompts or code.
- Do not disable Entire or remove its hooks.

## Commits
- The subject says what the product can now do: imperative, under ~60 characters.
- One logical change per commit.
- No AI attribution or co-author trailers. The `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is added
  automatically and must stay.
- No em dashes.

=== README.md
# DurHack 2026 agent framework (template)

A small framework for running many coding agents at once during a hackathon. Claude Code, Codex
and Cursor follow the same rules. GitHub Issues is the task queue, `./hq` is the CLI around it,
and [Entire](https://entire.com) records sessions, maps the codebase, keeps memory and runs reviews.

## Pre-event tooling disclosure
This repository is a template prepared before DurHack 2026. It holds tooling, agent rules, docs
and GitHub templates only: no product code. At kick-off we create a fresh submission repo from
this template (`gh repo create --template`). All product code is written during DurHack, in that
repo.

## Quickstart
- Humans: [docs/PLAYBOOK.md](docs/PLAYBOOK.md) (kick-off checklist, dispatching agents, onboarding).
- Agents: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the skills in [.agents/skills](.agents/skills).
- Hack context: [docs/hack/BRIEF.md](docs/hack/BRIEF.md), [docs/SPEC.md](docs/SPEC.md),
  [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md).
- First run in a clone: `entire enable`, then `./hq setup` (Windows: `hq.cmd setup`), then
  `./hq board`.

=== docs/DECISIONS.md
# Decisions

Append-only log, newest at the bottom. Add an entry when a choice would surprise a newcomer or is
costly to undo. Agents also record it with `entire brain remember "<decision>"`.

Format:

```
## YYYY-MM-DD: <decision>
**Context:** why it came up.
**Decision:** what we chose.
**Consequences:** what follows, good and bad.
```

## 2026-11-13: GitHub Issues is the single task queue
**Context:** Up to ~10 agents across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor need one shared view of the
work. A second tracker (beads, Backlog.md, Task Master) would drift from GitHub.
**Decision:** Every task is a GitHub issue in the task form. `./hq` claims, labels and ships them.
Humans dispatch; agents never pick their own.
**Consequences:** GitHub is the only shared state; `.context/` and workspaces are scratch. Every
agent needs `gh` auth and network access.

## 2026-11-13: Entire for sessions, memory and review
**Context:** We want shared session history, codebase mapping, persistent memory and cross-vendor
review, and we target Best Use of Entire. Entire's judging tool only reads `refs/heads/entire/*`.
**Decision:** Use Entire Sessions, Graph, Brain and Trails, and `entire review` (Claude Code and
Codex reviewers, one judge). Use the `branch` checkpoint backend.
**Consequences:** Every session is recorded and pushed, so no secrets in prompts. Each clone runs
`entire enable`. `review:pass` needs local `entire review`, hosted Trail review or `/hq-review`.

## 2026-11-13: Squash merges keep Entire-Checkpoint trailers
**Context:** Entire links commits to sessions through `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. A squash
message without them breaks the link.
**Decision:** Squash merge only. Repo setting: squash title = PR title, message = commit details.
`./hq ship` merges this way.
**Consequences:** `main` gets one commit per PR and `entire why` still resolves to sessions. Never
edit the trailers out of a squash message.

## 2026-11-13: Fresh submission repo from this template at kick-off
**Context:** MLH only judges work done during the event, and Entire's judging tool scores a clean
start higher.
**Decision:** This repo is a template. At kick-off we run `gh repo create --template` and hack in
the new repo.
**Consequences:** The submission has no pre-event history. Pre-kick-off agent sessions are closed
and fresh ones started. The README discloses the framework as pre-event tooling.

# hq-plan

1. Read `docs/hack/BRIEF.md`, `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/DECISIONS.md`.
   See what exists: `./hq board` and `gh issue list --state open`. Do not duplicate open issues.
2. Draft the issues. Rules:
   - 1 issue = 1 agent = 1 PR. Size S or M. Split anything L.
   - Issues that can run in parallel have disjoint Scope paths.
   - Contracts and skeleton first, in `M0 Skeleton`: shared types, API stubs, CI check commands
     (`check` in `hq.json`), deploy. Everything else is `Blocked by` them.
   - P0 = on the demo path in `docs/SPEC.md`. P1 = should have. P2 = nice to have.
   - Milestones: `M0 Skeleton`, `M1 MVP demo path`, `M2 Prizes + polish`, `M3 Submission`.
   - Each issue has one lane from `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, checkable acceptance criteria and exact
     Verify steps.
   - Titles are imperative and say what the product can do afterwards: they become commit subjects.
3. Show the human this table, then wait for approval. Revise until they approve.

   | # | Title | Lane | P | Size | Milestone | Scope | Blocked by |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

4. After approval, write each body to `.context/issue-<k>.md` with exactly these headings:

   ```markdown
   ### Goal
   ### Acceptance criteria
   ### Scope
   ### Do not touch
   ### Blocked by
   ### Verify
   ### Notes
   ```

   Blocked by is `#12, #14` or `none`. Scope and Do not touch list files or dirs.
5. Create blockers first so their numbers exist, then put the real numbers in each dependent's
   Blocked by. One command per issue:

   ```
   gh issue create --title "<title>" --body-file .context/issue-<k>.md \
     --label status:ready --label P1 --label size:S --label type:feat \
     --label lane:<x> --milestone "M0 Skeleton"
   ```

   Use `--label status:blocked` instead of `status:ready` when Blocked by is not `none`.
   A missing `lane:<x>` label means the lane is not in `hq.json`: ask the human.
6. Show `./hq board`. Do not claim or start anything: humans dispatch.

# Spec

What we build. `/hq-plan` turns it into issues. Business detail is in `docs/BUSINESS.md`, the
science and wording rules in `docs/DOMAIN.md`.

## Problem
The city measures night noise, but people feel it, and nobody connects the two. Newcastle's
Urban Observatory publishes kerbside noise levels and WHO publishes how night noise disturbs sleep,
yet a resident can't tell what woke them, and a traveller can't tell that a hotel overlooks a
24-hour demolition site. Bewick Court residents were kept awake until 5am by demolition under a
24-hour permit, and no open dataset recorded it.

## Product
Kip shows how the city's noise affects sleep, street by street, and turns that into a Quiet Stay
Score for every hotel in Newcastle. It has three layers:

| Layer | Feature | What the user sees |
|---|---|---|
| City | City sleep map | Each Observatory noise sensor shaded by an indicative % of nearby residents highly sleep disturbed |
| Personal | Personal night | Timeline of sleep stages, bedroom noise and wake-ups, each tagged with its likely cause |
| Personal | Morning briefing | Spoken summary on Watch or AirPods: "Two wake-ups followed drilling at 06:41, before the 8am limit" |
| Personal | Evidence log | An out-of-hours noise report for the council, its hash anchored on Solana |
| Business | Quiet Stays | Hotels ranked by predicted sleep quality for the traveller's profile, with booking links |

City map and Personal night are the core; the rest build on them.

## Users
- **Resident** near construction or nightlife: wants to know what wakes them and whether it broke
  the council's construction hours, with evidence they can send.
- **Traveller** choosing a Newcastle hotel: wants to know where they will sleep well, weighted for
  how they travel (light sleeper, night out, best value, business).
- **Judges**: see real city data, a real recorded night and one live noise event.

## Demo script (3 min)
One live moment carries the pitch: a drilling sound hits the phone, and Kip labels it, checks the
council's hours and briefs you within seconds.

| # | Time | Step | P |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0:00 | Hook: Bewick Court. "Where in Newcastle would you sleep worst tonight? Nobody can tell you. Kip can." | P0 |
| 2 | 0:20 | City map: real Observatory data, sensors shaded by an indicative 30-night estimate of residents highly sleep disturbed | P0 |
| 3 | 0:50 | Live noise event: phone on the table in demo mode (no Watch data). ElevenLabs-generated drilling clip played from a speaker held against it. Dashboard shows the spike, Gemini labels it "construction", Kip flags it as outside council hours, the ElevenLabs briefing plays | P0 |
| 4 | 1:40 | A real night recorded at home: sleep stages, bedroom noise, wake-ups, shown as counts against the random baseline | P0 |
| 5 | 2:10 | Quiet Stays: switch profile "Light sleeper" to "Night out", ranking reorders; a hotel penalised for works on the stay dates | P0 |
| 6 | 2:35 | Trust: edit a log, show it no longer matches its Solana memo. Flash `terraform plan` and the Entire session record | P1 |
| 7 | 2:50 | Business: affiliate commission now, Verified Quiet next, data licensing later | P0 (slide) |

If a P1 step isn't working at the freeze, cut it from the script rather than slip.

## MVP scope (M1)
- iOS app: relative dB logged once a second, a 10-second clip around each spike, on-device
  voice-activity check that drops clips with speech, recording while locked, HealthKit read of
  the Watch's sleep stages, heart rate, HRV and respiratory rate after the night ends, upload to
  the API, and a live demo mode that streams dB.
- Ingest worker: Observatory noise, NO2 and PM2.5 every 5 minutes, plus a backfill of at least
  30 nights; OpenStreetMap hotels and venues.
- API: night upload, clip labelling (Gemini, then delete the clip), wake-up attribution,

  ranking per profile, Street Manager SNS endpoint (or a recorded sample).
- Dashboard: city map, night timeline, live event view, Quiet Stays page.
- Deployed on Vultr via Terraform, HTTPS via Caddy on an sslip.io hostname.

## Non-goals
- Calibrated dB from the phone. Kip uses spikes relative to the night's own baseline.
- Room-level hotel scores. The score describes a hotel's surroundings.
- Claiming noise *caused* a wake-up. Kip shows a link.
- Real affiliate bookings. Demo links are placeholders.
- Building or demolition sites outside Street Manager, except as heard by the bedroom microphone.
- An all-night Watch workout session (drains 40% to 100% of the battery). Read HealthKit instead.

1. Solana Memo anchoring and the tamper demo (P1).
2. ElevenLabs Scribe as a second noise classifier; disagreements become "uncertain" (P1).
3. Complaint draft for the council from the evidence log (P1).

6. Air quality factor in the hotel score (P2).

- Does one of us sleep at home in Newcastle during the event, near an Observatory noise sensor?

# Business

How Kip makes money and what the Quiet Stay Score is. Read this for any work on hotels, scoring,
profiles or booking links. Scoring maths and wording rules are in `docs/DOMAIN.md`.

## Model
Kip recommends hotels on how well you'll sleep there and what's around them, and takes affiliate
commission on each booking. The same data that powers the city map and the personal night powers
the hotel ranking, so the business layer costs little extra to build.

## Quiet Stay Score (0 to 100)
One score per hotel, built from data Kip already collects. It describes the hotel's surroundings,
not a specific room: the side of the building and the floor can matter as much as the street.

| Input | Source | Effect on score |
|---|---|---|
| Indicative night-noise disturbance | Nearest Observatory noise sensors, distance-weighted, 30-night Lnight through the WHO road-traffic curve | Main factor |
| Active roadworks within 200 m | Street Manager permits; work scheduled at night (from proposed times and traffic management type) weighs more | Penalty for the dates of the stay only |
| Air quality at night | Observatory NO2 and PM2.5 | Small factor |
| Real nights nearby | Opted-in Kip users sleeping within 300 m | Corrects the estimate once there's enough data |
| Distance to nightlife and sights | OpenStreetMap venues | A preference, not a penalty (see profiles) |

### Profiles
Kip asks one question up front and re-weights the score.

| Profile | What Kip ranks first |
|---|---|
| Light sleeper | Lowest predicted disturbance |
| Night out | Within walking distance of nightlife, then quietest |
| Best value | Most quiet points per pound per night |
| Business | Quiet on weeknights, close to the station |

### Rules for the score
- It is an estimate and the UI says so. Every score has its sources one tap away: which sensors,
  which permits, how many real nights. Without this, low-scoring hotels will dispute it.
- Weights live in one place in `packages/shared` so the dashboard can show the breakdown.
- Simulated cohort nights are flagged and labelled wherever they affect a score.

## Revenue
1. **Affiliate commission (launch).** Booking links through affiliate networks. Booking.com cut
   thousands of smaller affiliates in 2025 and moved them to networks such as Awin and CJ;
   Expedia Group's affiliate programme and aggregators such as Travelpayouts are the other routes
   for a small team. Affiliate approval takes weeks, so the demo uses OpenStreetMap hotels with
   placeholder booking links. Don't quote a commission rate until it's confirmed.
2. **Verified Quiet (year one).** Hotels that already score well pay a yearly fee to replace the
   estimate with measured, room-by-room data from in-room sensors. Hotels that score badly get a
   free report showing which rooms and hours are the problem, as the route to a better score.
3. **Data licensing (later).** Area-level sleep disturbance data for councils, developers
   scheduling construction, and estate agents.

## Hypotheses, not findings
- Renters choosing a flat for a 12-month lease may be a bigger market than hotel guests: same
  score, higher stakes. Pitch it as the next market, not as evidence.

## Judge questions
| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is this real data? | The city map, the recorded night and the permits are real; other users are simulated and labelled on the map |
| Does noise cause the wake-ups? | We claim a link, not a cause: wake-ups follow spikes more often than random moments do, shown as counts until there are enough nights for a percentage |
| Can you use the WHO curve on kerbside sensors? | Only as an indication: the curve is for long-term road-traffic noise, so we average 30 nights and label the map indicative |
| How accurate is a phone microphone? | Not calibrated, so Kip uses spikes above the night's own baseline in relative dB. The city estimate uses Observatory sensors, which were validated against precision meters |
| Do you record people's bedrooms? | Clips with speech are dropped on the phone; other clips are deleted once labelled. Health data needs explicit consent under UK GDPR, and users can delete everything |
| Why Solana? | Cheap public timestamps on mainnet that a council can check without trusting Kip. They prove when a log existed, not that it's true |
| Why two databases? | Timestamped numbers in Tiger, documents and geo queries in MongoDB |
| Why would hotels pay? | Well-scoring hotels pay to swap the estimate for measured, room-level data; low scorers get a free report on what to fix |

## Sponsor mapping
All seven sponsors do real work in Kip. The prize table with targets is in `docs/hack/BRIEF.md`.

| Sponsor | Role in Kip | What to show the judges | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vultr | Compute, Container Registry and firewall, all provisioned by Terraform | `terraform plan`, then `terraform apply -replace=vultr_instance.api` rebuilding the server while the data stays put | Strong |
| MongoDB Atlas | Users, night summaries, hotels and scores; geo queries | The hotel ranking pipeline: `$geoNear` on hotels, then `$geoWithin` lookups for nearby sensors and works | Strong |
| Gemini | Labels noise clips, writes the briefing and complaint draft, on a paid-tier key | Play a drilling clip and a siren clip; show the two labels | Strong |
| Tiger Data | All time-series data and the 30-night Lnight per sensor | The continuous aggregate that turns raw readings into the city map | Strong |
| ElevenLabs | Briefing voice, Scribe as a second classifier, Sound Effects for the demo clip | The briefing playing on AirPods, and the two classifiers agreeing | Medium to strong |
| Solana | Writes each night's log hash to mainnet with the Memo program | Edit a log on stage, re-hash it, show it no longer matches the on-chain memo | Medium |
| Entire | Records every agent session | One slide showing the recorded reasoning behind a key commit | Free win |

# Domain

The science, rules and wording Kip depends on. Code that computes, labels or displays any of
these must follow this file. Constants live in `packages/shared`, not inline.

## Night noise and the WHO curve
- **Night window:** 23:00 to 07:00, `Europe/London` local time (handle BST changes).
- **Lnight:** the A-weighted equivalent level over the night window. It is an *energy* average,
  not an arithmetic mean of dB:
  `Lnight = 10 * log10(mean(10 ^ (L_i / 10)))`.
  In Tiger, average `power(10, db / 10)` and convert back with `10 * log10(...)`.
- **City estimate:** per sensor, the energy average of nightly Lnight over at least the last 30
  nights. Fewer than 30 nights: show the sensor as "not enough data", don't shade it.
- **WHO road-traffic curve** (Basner & McGuire 2018), % highly sleep disturbed:
  `%HSD = 19.4312 - 0.9336 * Lnight + 0.0126 * Lnight^2`.
  This reproduces the plan's figures (2.9% at 45 dB, 6.2% at 55 dB, 8.8% at 60 dB). Still check
  the paper before quoting more decimals.
- **Valid range:** 40 to 65 dB Lnight. Outside it, clamp for shading and mark the value as
  out of range; never extrapolate.
- **Thresholds** (WHO 2018): night-time road traffic below 45 dB Lnight, rail 44 dB, aircraft
  40 dB.
- **Limits:** the curve is for long-term road-traffic noise at a home's most exposed facade.
  Observatory sensors sit at the kerb and also pick up nightlife and voices. So the map is an
  *indicative road-traffic estimate*, never a measured disturbance rate.

## Bedroom noise (phone)
- The iPhone microphone is not calibrated. Store and show **relative dB** only.
- Sample once a second. A **spike** is a level above the night's own baseline (rolling median)
  by a threshold set in `packages/shared`. Keep a 10-second clip around each spike.
- On-device voice-activity check: any clip containing speech is dropped on the phone and never
  uploaded.

## Wake-up attribution
- **Wake-up signals:** a Watch "awake" stage during the sleep session, or a sudden heart-rate
  jump during sleep (Watch stages are coarse and miss brief arousals).
- **Method:** look for a spike in the 60 to 120 seconds before each wake-up, and compare the hit
  rate against randomly chosen windows of the same length from the same night.
- **Small numbers:** one night has 2 to 6 wake-ups. Show counts ("3 of 4 wake-ups followed a
  spike"). Show a percentage only once several nights are pooled from HealthKit history.
- HealthKit sleep stages appear only after the sleep session ends. Live demo mode needs no Watch
  data.

## Noise classification
- Labels: `construction`, `traffic`, `siren`, `snoring`, `other`, plus `uncertain`.
- Gemini (paid-tier key) labels each clip, with JSON output. ElevenLabs Scribe audio-event tags
  give a second opinion. Where they disagree, the event is `uncertain`. This stops a user's own
  snoring being blamed on the building site.
- The clip is deleted once labelled. Only the label is kept.

## Construction hours (Newcastle City Council)
Recommended hours for noisy construction work:

| Day | Allowed |
|---|---|
| Monday to Friday | 08:00 to 18:00 |
| Saturday | 08:00 to 13:00 |
| Sunday and bank holidays | None |

A `construction` event outside these hours is flagged "outside council hours". Bank holidays for
England come from `https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json` (`england-and-wales`). These are
*recommended* hours: say "outside the council's recommended hours", not "illegal".

## Street Manager
DfT Street Manager pushes street and road works permits in England (location, work category,
traffic management type, proposed and actual times) over AWS SNS to a public HTTPS endpoint. The
subscription must be confirmed within 3 days. It covers roads, not building or demolition sites.
Night work is inferred from proposed times and traffic management type.

## Evidence log and Solana
Each night's log is serialised canonically, hashed (SHA-256), and the hash written to Solana
mainnet with the Memo program (no Anchor). It proves *when* a log existed, not that its contents
are true. Never claim more.

## Wording rules
Anything user-facing, in the briefing prompt, the dashboard or the pitch:

| Say | Never say |
|---|---|
| "linked to", "followed" | "caused by" |
| "indicative estimate" | "measured disturbance", "% of residents are disturbed" |
| "outside the council's recommended hours" | "illegal", "breach" |
| "relative dB" for phone data | bare "dB" for phone data |
| "simulated" on cohort data | anything implying simulated users are real |
| "proves when the log existed" | "proves the noise happened" |

## Privacy (UK GDPR)
Sleep and heart data are special-category health data.
- Explicit, separate consent per data type: microphone, HealthKit, location.
- Store only relative dB, labelled events and HealthKit summaries. No raw audio at rest.
- Audio clips are deleted once labelled; clips with speech never leave the phone.
- One action deletes everything a user has, in both databases.
- Never log raw health values or audio in server logs.

# Architecture

Source of truth for stack, lanes and contracts. Change a contract only through its own issue.
Product context: `docs/SPEC.md`. Science and wording rules: `docs/DOMAIN.md`.

## Overview
One TypeScript API and one ingest worker, built from one Docker image, run on a Vultr instance in
London behind Caddy for HTTPS. Terraform provisions the instance, its firewall, the container
registry and the database access rules.

```
 iPhone (+ Watch via HealthKit)     Dashboard (browser)     Open data
  mic relative dB, clips,               |                  Observatory, OSM,
  sleep stages, vitals                  |                  Street Manager (SNS push)
        | upload                        |                       |            |
        v                               v                       | push       | pull every 5 min
 +--------------------------- Vultr, London -------------------------------------------+
 |  API (Hono, Caddy HTTPS, SNS endpoint, serves dashboard)  <--+   Ingest worker      |
 +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
        |            |              |            | reads/writes            | writes readings
        v            v              v            v                         v
     Gemini     ElevenLabs       Solana     +------------- Data stores ---------------+
   classify,    TTS, Scribe,     Memo       |  Tiger Data: noise, sensor readings,    |
   narrate      Sound Effects    hashes     |    sleep stages, vitals                 |
                                            |  MongoDB Atlas: users, night summaries, |
                                            |    hotels, sensors, works, scores       |
                                            +-----------------------------------------+
```

- The phone uploads each night to the API. In live demo mode it also streams dB samples.
- The worker pulls Observatory readings and OpenStreetMap venues every 5 minutes. The API receives
  Street Manager permits as they're pushed.
- **The API is the only thing that calls Gemini, ElevenLabs and Solana**, so keys live in one
  place. The iOS app and the dashboard never hold third-party keys.
- Every timestamped value goes in Tiger. MongoDB holds one summary document per night plus users,
  hotels, sensors, works and scores.

## Stack
| Layer | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| iOS app | Swift/SwiftUI, HealthKit, AVAudioRecorder metering, on-device voice-activity check, CoreLocation, background audio mode | Records while locked; reads Watch sleep data without a Watch app. Needs an Apple developer account and the HealthKit entitlement |
| watchOS (stretch) | SwiftUI: haptics, "something woke me", briefing playback | Only if Watch signing works in the first 2 hours |
| API and worker | TypeScript on Bun, Hono, Zod, node-cron; one image, two entrypoints | Hono also serves the Street Manager SNS endpoint and the dashboard build |
| Dashboard | React, Vite, MapLibre GL with OpenStreetMap tiles | Built to static files, served by the API |
| Time series | Tiger Data (TimescaleDB): hypertables plus continuous aggregates | Event-window and night-average queries |
| Documents | MongoDB Atlas with 2dsphere indexes | Hotel ranking is one aggregation pipeline |
| AI | Gemini API on a paid-tier key, JSON output | Free-tier keys aren't allowed for UK-facing apps |
| Voice | ElevenLabs TTS (briefing), Scribe (second classifier), Sound Effects (demo clip) | |
| Chain | Solana mainnet, Memo program only (no Anchor) | A memo costs a fraction of a penny |
| Hosting | Vultr Cloud Compute (London), Vultr Container Registry, Caddy with an `<ip>.sslip.io` hostname | iOS requires HTTPS; no domain needed |
| Infra | Terraform: `vultr/vultr`, `mongodb/mongodbatlas` (IP access list), Tiger Cloud provider; cloud-init via `templatefile()` | One command rebuilds the stack |
| Process | Entire in the repo from the first commit | Records every agent session |

`./hq check` runs the `check` commands in `hq.json` (lint, typecheck, tests). Keep it under ~2 min.
`./hq setup` runs the `setup` commands (install dependencies). Both are empty until M0 adds code.

## Repo layout
```
apps/ios/                 Kip iOS app (Xcode project, SwiftUI)
apps/server/              one TS package, one Docker image
  src/api/                Hono routes, SNS endpoint, static dashboard
  src/worker/             node-cron ingest jobs and backfills
  src/services/           clients: gemini, elevenlabs, solana, observatory, overpass, street-manager
  src/db/                 Tiger and Mongo clients, SQL migrations, index setup
apps/dashboard/           React + Vite + MapLibre
packages/shared/          Zod schemas (upload, API), domain constants, WHO curve, score weights
infra/                    Terraform, cloud-init.yaml.tftpl, Caddyfile
Dockerfile                builds apps/server and apps/dashboard into one image
```

## Lanes
A lane is a set of dirs. Both of us work across every lane; lanes exist so parallel issues touch
disjoint paths. They are mirrored in `hq.json`.

| Lane | Dirs | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `ios` | `apps/ios/` | Both |
| `api` | `apps/server/src/api/`, `apps/server/src/services/` | Both |
| `worker` | `apps/server/src/worker/`, `apps/server/src/db/` | Both |
| `web` | `apps/dashboard/` | Both |
| `infra` | `infra/`, `Dockerfile` | Both (Ellis merges, owns deploys) |
| `shared` | `packages/shared/` | Both (contracts: own issue each) |

## Contracts
Merge in M0, before anyone branches. Agree the upload JSON in the first 30 minutes so the iOS and
server tracks never block each other.

| Contract | Lives in | Owner lane |
|---|---|---|
| Night upload (phone to API) | `packages/shared/src/upload.ts` + Swift `Codable` mirror in `apps/ios` | `shared` |
| API routes and response shapes | `packages/shared/src/api.ts` | `shared` |
| Domain constants (night window, spike threshold, attribution window, construction hours, WHO curve) | `packages/shared/src/domain.ts` | `shared` |
| Quiet Stay Score inputs and weights per profile | `packages/shared/src/score.ts` | `shared` |
| Tiger schema | `apps/server/src/db/migrations/` | `worker` |
| Mongo collections and indexes | `apps/server/src/db/mongo.ts` | `worker` |

### Night upload (draft, settle at M0)
```ts
NightUpload = {
  nightId: uuid, userId: uuid,
  startedAt: ISODateTime, endedAt: ISODateTime,          // Europe/London offsets
  location?: { lat: number, lon: number },               // only with location consent
  consent: { microphone: boolean, health: boolean, location: boolean },
  noise: { baselineDb: number, samples: [t: epochSec, db: number][] },   // relative dB, 1 Hz
  spikes: { t: epochSec, peakDb: number, clipId?: string }[],
  sleep?: {                                              // absent in live demo mode
    stages: { start, end, stage: "inBed"|"awake"|"core"|"deep"|"rem" }[],
    heartRate: [t, bpm][], hrv: [t, ms][], respiratoryRate: [t, perMin][],
  },
}
```
Clips upload separately (`POST /v1/nights/:id/clips`) and are deleted after labelling.

### API routes (draft)
| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/nights` | Upload a night |
| `POST /v1/nights/:id/clips` | Upload one 10 s clip; returns labels; clip deleted |
| `GET /v1/nights/:id` | Timeline, events, attribution counts, hours flags |
| `GET /v1/nights/:id/briefing` | Briefing text and audio URL |
| `POST /v1/nights/:id/anchor`, `GET /v1/nights/:id/verify` | Solana memo write and hash check |
| `POST /v1/live/samples`, `GET /v1/live/stream` (SSE) | Live demo mode |
| `GET /v1/city/sensors` | Sensors with 30-night Lnight, %HSD, data status |
| `GET /v1/hotels?profile=&checkIn=&checkOut=` | Ranked hotels with score breakdown and sources |
| `POST /v1/street-manager/sns` | SNS subscription confirmation and permit notifications |
| `DELETE /v1/users/:id` | Delete everything for a user, in both stores |

## Data
### Tiger (TimescaleDB)
| Table | Kind | Key columns |
|---|---|---|
| `sensor_readings` | hypertable | `time, sensor_id, metric (noise_db, no2, pm25), value` |
| `night_noise` | hypertable | `time, night_id, db` (relative) |
| `sleep_stages` | table | `night_id, start, end, stage` |
| `vitals` | hypertable | `time, night_id, metric (hr, hrv, resp), value` |
| `sensor_lnight_daily` | continuous aggregate | Energy-averaged noise per sensor per night window (see `docs/DOMAIN.md`) |

The 30-night Lnight per sensor is a query over `sensor_lnight_daily`. Backfill at least 30 nights
of Observatory history in hour one.

### MongoDB Atlas
| Collection | Holds | Indexes |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | Consent, profile choice | |
| `nights` | One summary per night: events, labels, attribution counts, hours flags, log hash, memo signature | `userId, startedAt` |
| `sensors` | Observatory sensor, GeoJSON point, latest 30-night Lnight and %HSD | `2dsphere` |
| `hotels` | OSM hotel, GeoJSON point, placeholder booking link, `simulated` flags | `2dsphere` |
| `works` | Street Manager permits, geometry, proposed/actual times, night flag | `2dsphere` |
| `venues` | OSM nightlife and sights | `2dsphere` |

Hotel ranking is one pipeline: `$geoNear` on `hotels` first (only one is allowed, and it must be
the first stage), then `$lookup` with `$geoWithin` and `$centerSphere` into `sensors`, `works` and
`venues`, then the profile weights from `packages/shared`.

## Env vars
Secrets live in `.env`, never committed and never pasted into a prompt. Conductor copies `.env*`
into each new workspace via `.worktreeinclude`. For a plain git worktree, copy `.env` by hand.

| Name | Used by | Where to get it |
|---|---|---|
| `MONGO_URI` | API, worker | MongoDB Atlas cluster (MLH credit) |
| `TIGER_URI` | API, worker | Tiger Cloud service |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | API | Google AI Studio, **paid tier** (enable billing in hour one) |
| `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | API | ElevenLabs (MLH promo code) |
| `SOLANA_RPC_URL`, `SOLANA_KEYPAIR` | API | Mainnet RPC; a small funded keypair used only for memos |
| `STREET_MANAGER_TOPIC_ARN` | API | Street Manager open data registration (register in hour one) |
| `VULTR_API_KEY` | Terraform | Vultr account (MLH credit) |
| `MONGODB_ATLAS_PUBLIC_KEY`, `MONGODB_ATLAS_PRIVATE_KEY` | Terraform | Atlas org API key |
| Tiger Cloud provider credentials | Terraform | Tiger Cloud console; names per the provider docs |
| `TF_VAR_admin_ip` | Terraform | Your public IP, for SSH |

The iOS app only needs the API base URL (`https://<ip>.sslip.io`).

## Deploy
Ellis owns deploys. The demo runs from tag `demo-v1`.
- `infra/` holds Terraform: SSH key, private container registry, firewall (22 from `admin_ip`
  only; 80 and 443 open for Caddy), a `vc2-2c-4gb` Ubuntu 24.04 instance in `lhr`, and the Atlas IP
  access list for the instance's IP. Keys come from variables, never the repo.
- cloud-init installs Docker and Caddy, builds an `<ip>.sslip.io` hostname from instance
  metadata, then pulls and runs the image twice (API and worker).
- The API retries its database connections on boot, because the Atlas access list is applied
  after the instance exists.
- Demo: `terraform apply -replace=vultr_instance.api` rebuilds only the server; data stays put.
- To confirm against provider docs before relying on them: the Vultr region, the registry plan,
  and the registry `urn` attribute.

**Context:** Gemini, ElevenLabs and Solana need secret keys; the iOS app and dashboard are clients.
**Decision:** Only the API calls Gemini, ElevenLabs and Solana. Clients call the API.
**Consequences:** Keys live in one place. Clip labelling and briefings need a network round trip.

**Context:** Kip has dense timestamped data (1 Hz noise, sensor readings, vitals) and geo
documents (hotels, sensors, works). Both are sponsor tracks.
**Decision:** Every timestamped value goes in Tiger; MongoDB holds users, one summary per night,

centrepiece.
**Consequences:** Two stores to provision and delete from. User deletion must cover both.

**Context:** An all-night workout session drains 40% to 100% of a Watch battery, and Watch app
signing is a known time sink.
**Decision:** The iPhone reads the Watch's own sleep tracking from HealthKit after the night ends.

**Consequences:** Sleep stages arrive only after the session ends, so the live demo uses the

## 2026-11-14: Claim links, not causes; label estimates
**Context:** One night has 2 to 6 wake-ups, phone dB is uncalibrated, and the WHO curve is for
long-term road traffic at the facade, not kerbside sensors.

**Consequences:** Weaker-sounding claims that survive judge questions.

## 2026-11-14: Placeholder booking links for the demo
**Context:** Affiliate approval takes weeks; Booking.com cut small affiliates in 2025.
**Decision:** Hotels come from OpenStreetMap with placeholder booking links. Apply to a network
anyway and don't quote a commission rate until confirmed.
**Consequences:** Revenue is shown as the model, not as live bookings.

**Context:** We want cheap public timestamps a council can check without trusting Kip.
**Decision:** Hash each night's log and write it to mainnet with the Memo program. No Anchor, no
custom program.

I've written the Kip docs from the PDF and committed them as `1b3f176` on `docs/kip-business-architecture`, which branches from `origin/ehewes/new-conversation`. Nothing is pushed yet. The repo's hq tests pass (80/80), and the new lanes produce valid labels for `./hq bootstrap`.

**What changed**
- **`docs/SPEC.md`**: the problem, the three layers and five features, who the users are, the 3-minute demo script with a priority on each step, what's in the first build (M1), what we won't build, stretch goals, and the PDF's 4 open questions with their assumptions.
- **`docs/BUSINESS.md`** (new): the Quiet Stay Score inputs, the four traveller profiles, the three revenue streams, the renters idea marked as a guess to test, answers to likely judge questions, and what each sponsor does in Kip.
- **`docs/DOMAIN.md`** (new): the rules agents must follow. Kip shows indicative estimates, never measured rates; the WHO curve only applies between 40 and 65 dB; wake-ups are reported as counts; the council's construction hours; the privacy rules; and a "say / never say" table (for example "linked to", never "caused by").
- **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`**: the stack, a proposed repo layout, the 6 lanes, the shared contracts, draft upload JSON and API routes, the Tiger tables and Mongo collections, env vars, and the Terraform deploy.
- **`docs/hack/BRIEF.md`**: team and project filled in, the checkpoints, a target for each prize, the sign-ups to start in hour one, and the risk table.
- **`docs/DECISIONS.md`**: 8 new entries dated today.
- **`AGENTS.md` / `README.md`**: point to the new docs. `AGENTS.md` also gets 3 product rules for every agent.
- **`hq.json`**: lanes `ios`, `api`, `worker`, `web`, `infra` and `shared`, all owned by "both". The `check` and `setup` commands stay empty until there's code.

**Choices I made that the PDF didn't**
- **Bun as the runtime and package manager.** The API and worker live in one `apps/server` package with two entrypoints, which gives the PDF's single Docker image.
- **Lnight is a log average.** It has to average the sound energy, not the dB numbers, or it reads too low. The docs say this so agents don't get it wrong.
- **WHO curve formula.** The docs give `19.4312 - 0.9336·L + 0.0126·L²`. I checked that it gives the PDF's 2.9%, 6.2% and 8.8%.
- **Bank holidays** come from the gov.uk bank holidays JSON.
- **Upload JSON and API routes are drafts.** They're marked to settle in the first 30 minutes.
- **Quiet Stays is P0, Solana is P1.** The template says every demo step is P0, but the PDF says to cut scope rather than miss the freeze. So Solana and the Terraform flash (step 6) can be dropped at the freeze.
- **No numbers yet for the spike threshold or the score weights.** The PDF doesn't give any, so they're left as constants in `packages/shared` to tune.
- **Owners and deploys.** Lanes are owned by "both", as you said. I kept the template's rule that Ellis owns deploys and the `demo-v1` tag.

# Architecture

Source of truth for stack, file tree, lanes and contracts. Change a contract only through its own
issue. Product context: `docs/SPEC.md`. Science and wording rules: `docs/DOMAIN.md`.

## Overview
One Expo app builds both the iPhone app and the web dashboard used on stage. One TypeScript server
image runs two processes, the API (tRPC on Hono) and the ingest worker, on a Vultr instance in
London behind Caddy for HTTPS. Terraform provisions the instance, its firewall, the container
registry and the database access rules.

```
 Kip app (iOS)                      Kip app (web build)      Open data
  mic relative dB, clips,            city map, live event,   Observatory, OSM,
  HealthKit sleep + vitals           Quiet Stays             Street Manager (SNS push)
        | tRPC + clip upload               | tRPC                 |            |
        v                                  v                      | push       | pull every 5 min
 +--------------------------- Vultr, London -------------------------------------------+
 |  API: Hono + tRPC, Caddy HTTPS, SNS route, serves web build  <--+   Ingest worker   |
 +-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
        |            |              |            | reads/writes            | writes readings
        v            v              v            v                         v
     Gemini     ElevenLabs       Solana     +------------- Data stores ---------------+
   classify,    TTS, Scribe,     Memo       |  Tiger Data: noise, sensor readings,    |
   narrate      Sound Effects    hashes     |    sleep stages, vitals                 |
                                            |  MongoDB Atlas: users, night summaries, |
                                            |    hotels, sensors, works, scores       |
                                            +-----------------------------------------+
```

- The phone uploads each night through tRPC, and each spike clip through a plain upload route.
  In live demo mode it streams dB samples, and the web build subscribes to them.
- The worker pulls Observatory readings and OpenStreetMap venues every 5 minutes. The API receives
  Street Manager permits as they're pushed.
- **The API is the only thing that calls Gemini, ElevenLabs and Solana**, so keys live in one
  place. The app (iOS or web) never holds third-party keys.
- Every timestamped value goes in Tiger. MongoDB holds one summary document per night plus users,
  hotels, sensors, works and scores.

## Stack
Bun is the package manager and workspace tool everywhere, and the server runtime.

| Layer | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| App | React Native + TypeScript on Expo (SDK current at kick-off) with a dev client, Expo Router, TanStack Query + tRPC client | One codebase, two targets: iOS (the phone on the nightstand) and web (the demo dashboard). Needs an Apple developer account and the HealthKit entitlement |
| HealthKit | `@kingstinct/react-native-healthkit` with its Expo config plugin | Reads the Watch's sleep stages, heart rate, HRV and respiratory rate after the night ends |
| Audio | Local Expo Module `kip-audio` (Swift): AVAudioRecorder metering at 1 Hz, 10 s spike clips, on-device speech check (SoundAnalysis built-in classifier), background audio mode | No JS library does all of this reliably while locked; one small native module does |
| Map | MapLibre with OpenStreetMap tiles: `@maplibre/maplibre-react-native` on iOS, `maplibre-gl` on web, behind one `Map` component split by `.native.tsx` / `.web.tsx` | |
| watchOS (stretch) | Native SwiftUI watch target: haptics, "something woke me", briefing playback | Only if Watch signing works in the first 2 hours |
| API | TypeScript, tRPC v11 on Hono (`@hono/trpc-server`), Zod, SuperJSON | tRPC for every JSON call and the live subscription (SSE). Plain Hono routes only for binary clip upload, the Street Manager SNS endpoint, health check and the web build |
| Worker | TypeScript, node-cron, same image as the API | Runs each feature's jobs |
| Time series | Tiger Data (TimescaleDB): hypertables plus continuous aggregates | Event-window and night-average queries |
| Documents | MongoDB Atlas with 2dsphere indexes | Hotel ranking is one aggregation pipeline |
| AI | Gemini API on a paid-tier key, JSON output | Free-tier keys aren't allowed for UK-facing apps |
| Voice | ElevenLabs TTS (briefing), Scribe (second classifier), Sound Effects (demo clip) | |
| Chain | Solana mainnet, Memo program only (no Anchor) | A memo costs a fraction of a penny |
| Hosting | Vultr Cloud Compute (London), Vultr Container Registry, Caddy with an `<ip>.sslip.io` hostname | iOS requires HTTPS; no domain needed |
| Infra | Terraform: `vultr/vultr`, `mongodb/mongodbatlas` (IP access list), Tiger Cloud provider; cloud-init via `templatefile()` | One command rebuilds the stack |
| Quality | Biome (lint + format), `tsc -b` (typecheck), `bun test` | `./hq check` runs these once M0 adds them to `hq.json` |
| Process | Entire in the repo from the first commit | Records every agent session |

`./hq check` runs the `check` commands in `hq.json`. Keep it under ~2 min.
`./hq setup` runs the `setup` commands (`bun install`). Both are empty until M0 adds code.

## File tree
The tree is split **by feature first, then by layer**, so several agents can build different
features at once without touching the same files. A feature is one product capability end to end:
its screens, its tRPC router, its business logic, its jobs, its schemas and its tests.

```
apps/
  mobile/                         Expo app: iOS + web
    app/                          Expo Router routes. Thin: each file renders one feature screen
      _layout.tsx                 providers (tRPC, query client), written in M0
      (tabs)/_layout.tsx          tab list, written in M0 with every tab stubbed
      (tabs)/index.tsx            -> features/city
      (tabs)/night.tsx            -> features/night
      (tabs)/stays.tsx            -> features/stays
      live.tsx                    -> features/live
      ...
    src/
      features/
        <feature>/
          screens/                full screens, imported by app/
          components/             feature-only components
          hooks/                  tRPC queries and mutations for this feature
          native/                 device APIs; platform files *.ios.ts / *.web.ts
          index.ts                the feature's public exports
      lib/
        trpc.ts                   tRPC client, links, base URL
        ui/                       shared primitives (Button, Card, Text, theme)
        map/                      Map.native.tsx, Map.web.tsx
    modules/
      kip-audio/                  local Expo Module (Swift + TS bindings)
    app.config.ts                 plugins, permission strings, background modes
  server/                         one package, one Docker image, two entrypoints
    src/
      main.api.ts                 Hono app: /trpc, /upload/clip, /sns/street-manager, /health, web build
      main.worker.ts              registers every feature's jobs with node-cron
      env.ts                      Zod-validated environment
      trpc/
        init.ts                   initTRPC, context, procedures
        router.ts                 appRouter: one line per feature router, written in M0
      features/
        <feature>/
          router.ts               tRPC procedures. Thin: validate, call the service
          service.ts              business logic; the only thing other features may call
          repo.ts                 this feature's Tiger and Mongo queries
          jobs.ts                 optional cron jobs, exported as a list
          http.ts                 optional plain Hono routes (upload, SNS)
          *.test.ts               colocated tests
          index.ts                exports router, jobs, and the service functions others may use
      integrations/               one client per external API: gemini.ts, elevenlabs.ts,
                                  solana.ts, observatory.ts, overpass.ts, street-manager.ts
      db/
        tiger.ts, mongo.ts        clients; retry on boot
        migrations/               SQL, one file per change, timestamp-prefixed
        indexes.ts                Mongo collections and indexes
packages/
  shared/                         pure TypeScript, no IO; used by app and server
    src/
      <feature>/                  Zod schemas and types for that feature's inputs and outputs
      domain/                     WHO curve, Lnight, construction hours, attribution maths,
                                  score weights, wording strings, each with tests
infra/                            Terraform, cloud-init.yaml.tftpl, Caddyfile
Dockerfile                        builds server + Expo web export into one image
```

The app gets end-to-end types from `import type { AppRouter } from "@kip/server/trpc/router"`.
It never imports server runtime code.

### Features
| Feature | App (`apps/mobile/src/features/`) | Server (`apps/server/src/features/`) | What it owns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `city` | City map screen | Sensors query, Observatory ingest job | 30-night Lnight and %HSD per sensor |
| `night` | Recording, upload, night timeline | Night upload, timeline query | Night documents and noise samples |
| `attribution` | Wake-up markers and counts on the timeline | Wake-up detection, spike vs random-window counts | Attribution results on a night |
| `labels` | Label chips on events | Clip upload route, Gemini + Scribe labelling, clip deletion | Event labels, `uncertain` logic |
| `briefing` | Briefing player | Gemini narrative, ElevenLabs TTS | Briefing text and audio |
| `evidence` | Evidence log, council report, verify view | Log hashing, Solana memo, complaint draft | Hashes, memo signatures |
| `stays` | Quiet Stays list, profile picker, score breakdown | Hotel ranking pipeline, OSM hotels and venues job | Hotels, venues, scores |
| `works` | Works layer on the map | Street Manager SNS route, permit storage | Works documents |
| `live` | Live demo screen (iOS sender, web viewer) | Live sample mutation and subscription | Live session state (in memory) |
| `account` | Onboarding, consent, delete everything | User, consent, profile, cascade delete | Users |

Construction-hours checks and the WHO curve live in `packages/shared/src/domain/`, since several
features and both apps use them.

### Rules that keep parallel agents apart
1. **Stay in your feature.** An issue names one feature. Its agent edits only that feature's
   folders in `apps/mobile`, `apps/server` and `packages/shared`, plus a new migration file.
2. **No reaching into another feature.** Import another feature only through its `index.ts`, and
   only service functions it exports. Never import its `repo.ts`, components or hooks. Need more
   from it? Open an issue for that feature.
3. **Registries are written once, in M0.** `trpc/router.ts`, `main.worker.ts`,
   `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` and the routes in `app/` are created with every feature stubbed, so
   feature work never edits them. Adding a feature later is its own issue.
4. **Shared code changes through its own issue:** `lib/ui`, `lib/map`, `trpc/init.ts`,
   `integrations/`, `db/` clients, `packages/shared/src/domain/`, `modules/kip-audio`,
   `app.config.ts`. Adding a new file in `integrations/` is fine; changing an existing one is not.
5. **Conflict-free by construction:** migrations are named
   `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<feature>_<what>.sql`; `env.ts` and `.env.example` take one line per variable,
   grouped by feature; never hand-merge `bun.lock`, rerun `bun install` instead.
6. **Platform splits by filename**, not `if (Platform.OS)` branches: `foo.ios.ts` and `foo.web.ts`.
   iOS-only features (recording, HealthKit) ship a `.web.ts` stub that renders "Open on iPhone".

## Lanes
Lanes are features. Both of us work across every lane; lanes exist so parallel issues touch
disjoint paths. Each lane covers that feature's folder in `apps/mobile/src/features/`,
`apps/server/src/features/` and `packages/shared/src/`. They are mirrored in `hq.json`.

| Lane | Dirs | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `city`, `night`, `attribution`, `labels`, `briefing`, `evidence`, `stays`, `works`, `live`, `account` | `*/features/<lane>/`, `packages/shared/src/<lane>/` | Both |
| `platform` | `apps/mobile/app/`, `apps/mobile/src/lib/`, `apps/mobile/modules/`, `apps/mobile/app.config.ts`, `apps/server/src/{trpc,integrations,db}/`, `apps/server/src/main.*.ts`, `apps/server/src/env.ts`, `packages/shared/src/domain/` | Both (one issue at a time) |
| `infra` | `infra/`, `Dockerfile` | Both (Ellis merges, owns deploys) |

## Contracts
Merge in M0, before anyone branches. Agree the night upload schema in the first 30 minutes so
recording and server work never block each other.

| Contract | Lives in | Owner lane |
|---|---|---|
| Night upload schema | `packages/shared/src/night/upload.ts` | `night` |
| Each feature's tRPC inputs and outputs | `packages/shared/src/<feature>/`, used by `features/<feature>/router.ts` | that feature |
| tRPC context, procedures, root router | `apps/server/src/trpc/` | `platform` |
| Domain constants (night window, spike threshold, attribution window, construction hours, WHO curve, score weights) | `packages/shared/src/domain/` | `platform` |
| `kip-audio` JS API | `apps/mobile/modules/kip-audio/index.ts` | `platform` |
| Tiger schema | `apps/server/src/db/migrations/` | the feature in the file name |
| Mongo collections and indexes | `apps/server/src/db/indexes.ts` | `platform` |

### Night upload (draft, settle at M0)
```ts
NightUpload = z.object({
  nightId: z.string().uuid(), userId: z.string().uuid(),
  startedAt: z.string().datetime({ offset: true }),       // Europe/London offsets
  endedAt: z.string().datetime({ offset: true }),
  location: z.object({ lat: z.number(), lon: z.number() }).optional(), // location consent only
  consent: z.object({ microphone: z.boolean(), health: z.boolean(), location: z.boolean() }),
  noise: z.object({ baselineDb: z.number(), samples: z.array(z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])) }), // [epochSec, relative dB], 1 Hz
  spikes: z.array(z.object({ t: z.number(), peakDb: z.number(), clipId: z.string().optional() })),
  sleep: z.object({                                       // absent in live demo mode
    stages: z.array(z.object({ start: z.string(), end: z.string(),
      stage: z.enum(["inBed", "awake", "core", "deep", "rem"]) })),
    heartRate: z.array(z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])),
    hrv: z.array(z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])),
    respiratoryRate: z.array(z.tuple([z.number(), z.number()])),
  }).optional(),
})
```

### tRPC routers (draft)
| Router | Procedures |
|---|---|
| `night` | `upload` (mutation), `get`, `list` |
| `labels` | `forNight`; clip bytes go to plain `POST /upload/clip`, which labels and then deletes them |
| `attribution` | `forNight` |
| `briefing` | `get` (text and audio URL) |
| `evidence` | `anchor` (mutation), `verify`, `report` |
| `live` | `push` (mutation), `stream` (subscription over SSE) |
| `city` | `sensors` |
| `stays` | `rank({ profile, checkIn, checkOut, near? })` |
| `works` | `near`; permits arrive on plain `POST /sns/street-manager` |
| `account` | `me`, `setConsent`, `setProfile`, `deleteEverything` |

Auth for the hackathon: the app generates a user ID on first launch and sends it as a header;
`trpc/init.ts` puts it on the context. No accounts or passwords.

## Data
### Tiger (TimescaleDB)
| Table | Kind | Key columns | Feature |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sensor_readings` | hypertable | `time, sensor_id, metric (noise_db, no2, pm25), value` | `city` |
| `sensor_lnight_daily` | continuous aggregate | Energy-averaged noise per sensor per night window (see `docs/DOMAIN.md`) | `city` |
| `night_noise` | hypertable | `time, night_id, db` (relative) | `night` |
| `sleep_stages` | table | `night_id, start, end, stage` | `night` |
| `vitals` | hypertable | `time, night_id, metric (hr, hrv, resp), value` | `night` |

The 30-night Lnight per sensor is a query over `sensor_lnight_daily`. Backfill at least 30 nights
of Observatory history in hour one.

### MongoDB Atlas
| Collection | Holds | Indexes | Feature |
|---|---|---|---|
| `users` | Consent, profile choice | | `account` |
| `nights` | One summary per night: events, labels, attribution counts, hours flags, log hash, memo signature | `userId, startedAt` | `night` (others add fields through its service) |
| `sensors` | Observatory sensor, GeoJSON point, latest 30-night Lnight and %HSD | `2dsphere` | `city` |
| `hotels` | OSM hotel, GeoJSON point, placeholder booking link, `simulated` flags | `2dsphere` | `stays` |
| `venues` | OSM nightlife and sights | `2dsphere` | `stays` |
| `works` | Street Manager permits, geometry, proposed/actual times, night flag | `2dsphere` | `works` |

Hotel ranking is one pipeline: `$geoNear` on `hotels` first (only one is allowed, and it must be
the first stage), then `$lookup` with `$geoWithin` and `$centerSphere` into `sensors`, `works` and
`venues`, then the profile weights from `packages/shared/src/domain/`.

## Env vars
Secrets live in `.env`, never committed and never pasted into a prompt. Conductor copies `.env*`
into each new workspace via `.worktreeinclude`. For a plain git worktree, copy `.env` by hand.

| Name | Used by | Where to get it |
|---|---|---|
| `MONGO_URI` | API, worker | MongoDB Atlas cluster (MLH credit) |
| `TIGER_URI` | API, worker | Tiger Cloud service |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | API | Google AI Studio, **paid tier** (enable billing in hour one) |
| `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | API | ElevenLabs (MLH promo code) |
| `SOLANA_RPC_URL`, `SOLANA_KEYPAIR` | API | Mainnet RPC; a small funded keypair used only for memos |
| `STREET_MANAGER_TOPIC_ARN` | API | Street Manager open data registration (register in hour one) |
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` | App | `https://<ip>.sslip.io`, or the local server in development. Not a secret |
| `VULTR_API_KEY` | Terraform | Vultr account (MLH credit) |
| `MONGODB_ATLAS_PUBLIC_KEY`, `MONGODB_ATLAS_PRIVATE_KEY` | Terraform | Atlas org API key |
| Tiger Cloud provider credentials | Terraform | Tiger Cloud console; names per the provider docs |
| `TF_VAR_admin_ip` | Terraform | Your public IP, for SSH |

Only `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` variables reach the app, and they end up in the bundle: never put a key there.

## Deploy
Ellis owns deploys. The demo runs from tag `demo-v1`.
- `infra/` holds Terraform: SSH key, private container registry, firewall (22 from `admin_ip`
  only; 80 and 443 open for Caddy), a `vc2-2c-4gb` Ubuntu 24.04 instance in `lhr`, and the Atlas IP

result.output:
# Playbook (humans)

How the two of us run DurHack with 6 to 10 agents. Agents follow `AGENTS.md`. This file is for us.

## Roles
- **Ellis** owns `main` and the demo build: deploys, the code freeze, the `demo-v1` tag.
- **Both** own lanes (see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`) and merge their own lane's PRs.
- **Humans dispatch.** Agents never pick or self-assign issues.

## Cheat sheet
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
## Kick-off checklist (~15 min at event start)
1. Create the submission repo from the template and invite the teammate:
   ```
   gh repo create ehewes/<name> --private --template ehewes/durhack-proj --clone
   gh api -X PUT repos/ehewes/<name>/collaborators/<teammate-login> -f permission=push
   ```
   Add the repo to Conductor and set its setup script to `./hq setup`.
2. In the new clone, each person runs `entire enable`. Git hooks are per clone; the settings with
   the `branch` checkpoint backend are already committed. Ellis links the repo on entire.com for
   Trails.
3. Ellis runs `./hq bootstrap` (labels, milestones, merge settings, ruleset). Then each machine
   runs `./hq setup`.
4. Codex users approve the hooks once (`/hooks`). Close **every** pre-kick-off agent session and
   start fresh ones: old sessions would date the timeline before kick-off.
**Overnight (optional)**
- One unattended agent loop on one self-contained ticket, off the demo path, with turn and
  budget limits (for example `claude -p "work on #N" --max-budget-usd 5`). Review it in the morning.

**Freeze (~3h before judging)**
- Ellis tags the known-good build and deploys it:
  `git fetch origin && git tag demo-v1 origin/main && git push origin demo-v1`.
- After the freeze only demo-path fixes merge, each rehearsed on the demo script. Tag `demo-v2`
  if one lands.

**Submission**
- `review:pass` can come from:
  - local `entire review` (needs the `claude` and `codex` CLIs);
  - hosted Trail review agents on entire.com (optional, needs credits: MLH promo code);
  - the other human's agent running `/hq-review <PR>`.
- Lane owners merge their own lane's PRs: tell the agent "ship it", or run `./hq ship <PR>`.
- Contracts, deploy config and anything after the freeze: Ellis merges.

## Rate limits and tokens
- Spread agents across the Claude, OpenAI and Cursor subscriptions. When one rate-limits,
## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `entire status`: Codex hooks not active | Fast-forward the root checkout: `git -C <root checkout> pull --ff-only` (Conductor: `~/conductor/repos/<name>`) |
| Commit on `main` blocked | Create a branch: `git switch -c <login>/N-slug`. `HQ_ALLOW_MAIN=1` is for emergencies, by the main owner only |
| `./hq ship` refused | Read the gate it names (CI, review, draft, conflicts), fix it, retry. Never bypass |
| `./hq claim` refused | The issue is closed, blocked or claimed by someone else. Check `./hq board` |

---
name: anti-slop
description: Rejects glassmorphism, rainbow CTAs, cartoon empty states, and SaaS visual clutter. Use when reviewing AI-generated UI, polishing visuals, or removing decorative noise.
title: Anti Slop
category: visual-taste
severity: hard-rule
references:
- reference/slop-checklist.md
---

If `.ux-profile.md` exists at the project root, read it before changing layout, color, or type.

### Intent

AI-generated and template-driven UI converges on the same clichés: rainbow buttons, frosted glass panels, cartoon empty states, and decorative chrome that adds no function. This skill bans those patterns so interfaces stay purposeful, readable, and aligned with the rest of the visual-taste skills.

### Hard Rules (Non-Negotiable)

- **No multi-color radial rainbow gradients on standard CTA buttons.** Primary actions use a solid fill or a single-hue subtle gradient (same hue, ≤10% lightness shift). Ban `conic-gradient`, multi-stop rainbow `linear-gradient`, and purple-to-orange radial fills on default buttons.
- **No glassmorphic blur (`backdrop-filter`) without high-contrast boundary.** If blur is used at all, the panel must have a visible 1px border ≥3:1 against whatever shows through, opaque fallback when `backdrop-filter` unsupported, and sufficient text contrast. Default product UI should omit blur entirely.
- **No generic cartoon vector people** (waving, high-fiving, empty-box mascots) in empty states. Use text, actionable CTAs, simple monochrome icons, or product-relevant screenshots — not stock illustration people.
- **No icons inside inputs unless functional.** Allowed: search magnifier, clear/reset control, password visibility toggle. Banned: decorative leading icons on every text field, emoji-style adorners, brand icons inside standard inputs.
- **No unnecessary pill containers around standard text metadata.** Timestamps, author names, file sizes, and tags render as plain text or minimal chips only when they are interactive filters. Do not wrap static metadata in rounded pastel pills for decoration.
- **Anti-slop deletes decoration, not structure.** Remove pills, glass, cartoons, and decorative chrome. Do **not** delete the list frame, row dividers, or search chrome. An empty-looking table after a slop pass is a **fail**, not a pass.

### Design Heuristics & Taste Principles

- When a element's only job is decoration, delete it.
- Prefer one neutral border and whitespace over gradients, blobs, and floating shapes.
- Empty states sell the next action, not illustration budget.
- If it appears in a generic SaaS landing template, assume it is slop until proven functional.
- Cross-check `.ux-profile.md` banned list — it may extend these rules.

### Concrete Scenarios (Before vs. After)

#### ❌ Anti-Pattern

Sign-up uses a `conic-gradient` "Get Started" button. Login form inputs each have a leading gray icon. Empty project view shows a cartoon character high-fiving. Settings show "Last updated" inside a lavender pill. A modal uses `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)` with no border on a busy background.

#### ✅ Best Practice

Primary CTA is solid accent fill. Search field keeps one magnifier icon; other fields are label + input only. Empty state: heading, one sentence of value, "Create project" button, optional simple 24px monochrome icon. Metadata runs as 12px secondary text. Modal uses opaque L3 surface, 1px border, optional scrim — no blur.

### Framework-Agnostic Implementation Blueprint

**Audit pass (grep / search changed files):**

```
backdrop-filter
conic-gradient
linear-gradient.*(#.*,#.*,#)   /* multi-hue gradients on buttons */
illustration|empty-state.*svg  /* review for cartoon people */
border-radius: 999             /* pill wrappers on static text */
```

**Replace patterns:**

```css
/* ❌ Slop */
.btn-primary {
  background: conic-gradient(from 180deg, #f00, #ff0, #0f0, #00f, #f0f);
}
.panel {
  backdrop-filter: blur(16px);
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2);
}

/* ✅ Restrained */
.btn-primary {
  background: var(--accent);
}
.panel {
  background: var(--surface-l3);
  border: 1px solid var(--border-l2);
}
```

Use [reference/slop-checklist.md](reference/slop-checklist.md) for the full identification matrix.

### Agent Checklist

- [ ] Read `.ux-profile.md` if present; merge its ban list with this skill.
- [ ] Scan CTAs — no rainbow or multi-hue radial gradients.
- [ ] Scan overlays — no unbounded glassmorphism; border + opaque fallback if blur exists.
- [ ] Scan empty states — no cartoon people illustrations.
- [ ] Scan inputs — icons only where functional (search, clear, toggle).
- [ ] Scan metadata — no decorative pill wrappers on static text.
- [ ] After a slop pass: list frame, row dividers, and search chrome still present — an empty-looking table is a fail.
- [ ] Run slop checklist matrix on any AI-generated or imported component.

# Slop Checklist — Visual Identification Matrix

Use this matrix during review of AI-generated or template UI. If **Detect** is true and **Allowed exception** is false, remove or rewrite the pattern.

## Forbidden CSS and layout clichés

| ID | Pattern | Detect (search / signal) | Allowed exception | Fix |
|----|---------|--------------------------|-------------------|-----|
| S1 | Rainbow CTA gradient | `conic-gradient`, or `linear-gradient` with ≥3 hues on `.btn`, `[role="button"]`, primary submit | Marketing hero **outside** app shell, explicitly in profile | Solid `--accent` or single-hue gradient |
| S2 | Purple-orange SaaS gradient | `#6366f1` → `#ec4899` or similar on buttons/backgrounds | None in app UI | Neutral canvas + accent solid |
| S3 | Glassmorphism panel | `backdrop-filter: blur(` without `border: 1px solid` ≥3:1 | None by default; profile may allow with strict boundary | Opaque L2/L3 surface + border |
| S4 | Frosted sidebar | Semi-transparent nav + blur over content | None | Opaque L1 surface, border-right |
| S5 | Decorative blob backgrounds | Large absolute `border-radius: 50%` blurred divs behind forms | Brand marketing pages only | Remove or replace with flat L0 |
| S6 | Neon glow border | `box-shadow: 0 0 20px` saturated hue on cards/inputs | None | 1px subtle border per elevation tokens |
| S7 | Hard drop-shadow cards | `rgba(0,0,0,0.2+)`, offset ≥8px, blur <12px | None | Border-first; shadow alpha <0.08 |
| S8 | Floating pastel pill tags on static text | `border-radius: 9999px` + pastel bg on non-interactive metadata | Interactive filter chips user can toggle | Plain secondary text or real chip component |
| S9 | Icon in every input | Leading SVG/icon on text, email, password fields | Search, clear, visibility toggle only | Remove decorative icons |
| S10 | Cartoon empty-state people | Illustration keywords: waving, high-five, team celebration, `undraw`, `:person` hero art | None | Text + CTA + optional 24px monochrome icon |
| S11 | Giant centered spinner empty page | Full-viewport loader as empty state | Initial app boot only, <1s | Actionable empty state pattern |
| S12 | Nested gradient borders | `padding: 2px` + gradient wrapper on cards | None | 1px solid `--border-subtle` |
| S13 | Over-rounded everything | `border-radius: 24px+` on inputs, tables, and buttons together | Brand profile explicitly specifies | Match system radius token (usually 6–8px UI) |
| S14 | Gradient text headings | `background-clip: text` rainbow on H1/H2 in app UI | Marketing hero only | Solid foreground color |
| S15 | Duplicate shadow + gradient + blur | Same component uses all three | None | Pick one depth mechanism (border first) |

## Quick grep patterns

```bash
# Run against changed CSS/component files
rg -i "backdrop-filter|conic-gradient" .
rg -i "linear-gradient\([^)]*#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}[^)]*#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}[^)]*#" .
rg -i "border-radius:\s*999" .
rg -i "box-shadow:.*0\.[2-9]|box-shadow:.*rgba\(0,\s*0,\s*0,\s*0\.[2-9]" .
```

## Component-level review

| Component | Slop signals | Clean alternative |
|-----------|--------------|-------------------|
| Primary button | Rainbow gradient, oversized radius, glow | Solid accent, 6–8px radius, medium weight label |
| Card | Glass background, heavy shadow, gradient border | L1 surface, 1px border, optional soft shadow |
| Empty state | Cartoon people, long paragraph, no CTA | Title + 1 sentence + verb-first button |
| Form field | Icon left, placeholder as label, pill error toast | Visible label, blur validation, inline error text |
| Modal | Blur backdrop only, no scrim opacity | Scrim 50–70% + opaque L3 panel + border |
| Nav item | Gradient active pill + icon + badge dot | Text + subtle bg or left border active indicator |

## Severity actions

| Result | Action |
|--------|--------|
| Any S1–S5 on core app path | **Block** — rewrite before merge |
| S6–S9 on secondary screens | **Fix** in same pass |
| S10–S15 | **Fix** unless profile documents exception |

## Profile integration

If `.ux-profile.md` **Banned anti-aesthetics** lists extra items, treat them as **hard-rule** equals to this matrix. Profile bans win when stricter.

## Sign-off

Reviewer confirms:

- [ ] No S1–S5 matches in application shell
- [ ] Empty states are actionable, not illustrative clutter
- [ ] Inputs contain only functional icons
- [ ] Metadata is not pill-wrapped for decoration
- [ ] Depth uses borders/shadows from elevation tokens, not glow/blur stacks

I've switched the architecture diagram to Mermaid and added the anti-slop skill for all agents. Both are pushed to PR #7 as `7e1422f`, and I updated the PR description. I couldn't check that the diagram renders: the step that ran mermaid-cli was blocked by the permission check, so look at it on the PR's file view.

import pathlib

sub("apps/server/src/main.api.ts", 'import { ensureIndexes } from "./db/indexes";\n', 'import { ensureIndexes } from "./db/indexes";\nimport { migrate } from "./db/migrate";\n')

cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
# One image, two processes: the API (default) and the worker
# (`bun apps/server/src/main.worker.ts`). The API also serves the Expo web build.
FROM oven/bun:1.4 AS install
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json bun.lock bunfig.toml ./
COPY apps/server/package.json apps/server/
COPY apps/mobile/package.json apps/mobile/
COPY packages/shared/package.json packages/shared/
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile

FROM install AS web
COPY tsconfig.base.json ./
COPY packages/shared packages/shared
COPY apps/mobile apps/mobile
# Empty API URL: the web build calls the API on its own origin
ENV EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=""
RUN cd apps/mobile && CI=1 bun x expo export --platform web --output-dir dist

FROM oven/bun:1.4 AS server-deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json bun.lock bunfig.toml ./
COPY apps/server/package.json apps/server/
COPY apps/mobile/package.json apps/mobile/
COPY packages/shared/package.json packages/shared/
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile --production --filter @kip/server

FROM oven/bun:1.4-slim
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production WEB_DIST=/app/web PORT=3000
COPY --from=server-deps /app/node_modules node_modules
COPY package.json tsconfig.base.json ./
COPY packages/shared packages/shared
COPY apps/server apps/server
COPY --from=web /app/apps/mobile/dist web
USER bun
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["bun", "apps/server/src/main.api.ts"]
EOF

content.text:
I've built the boilerplate, setup and CI on a new branch, `feat/boilerplate-setup` (off `main`), in 5 commits. `./hq check` passes locally (lint, typecheck across all 3 packages, 15 tests). The GitHub Actions workflow itself hasn't run yet because nothing is pushed.

**What I ran locally**
- The Docker image builds. Against local databases it served `/health`, the web app (including deep links like `/night`) and tRPC, and it applied migrations on boot. The worker starts.
- Terraform passes `fmt -check` and `validate`, run through the official Terraform image because it isn't installed on this Mac.
- The Expo web export builds and picks up `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` from the root `.env`.

**What's in it**
- **Workspace:** Bun workspaces, Biome, a shared TypeScript config, `.env.example`, and `compose.yaml` running TimescaleDB and MongoDB for local work. TypeScript is pinned to ~6.0.3 everywhere, because Expo SDK 58 expects it (Bun had installed 7.0).
- **`packages/shared`:** the domain maths from `docs/DOMAIN.md` with tests: the WHO curve (it reproduces 2.9%, 6.2% and 8.8%), the Lnight energy average, and construction hours in London time including BST and bank holidays. Also the draft night upload schema, and a folder for each feature.
- **`apps/server`:** Hono + tRPC with all 10 feature routers registered once. The worker's job list and the plain routes (`/upload/clip` and `/sns/street-manager`, which return 501 for now) are registered the same way. Database connections retry on boot; Tiger migrations and Mongo indexes run when the API starts.
- **`apps/mobile`:** Expo Router with tabs for City, Night, Stays and Account, plus Live and Evidence screens. Each route is a one-line file that renders its feature's screen. The tRPC client gets its types from the server, and there's a small neutral UI kit that follows anti-slop.
- **`Dockerfile`:** one image. It runs the API by default, which also serves the web build, or the worker.
- **`infra/`:** Terraform from the plan, plus cloud-init that runs the API, the worker and Caddy on an `<ip>.sslip.io` hostname.
- **CI:** three jobs. `checks` runs the hq tests, `./hq setup --ci` and `./hq check`; `terraform` runs format and validate; `docker` builds the image.
- **Docs:** `hq.json` now has real setup and check commands, and the `platform` lane covers the new shared files. `README.md` has run instructions and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` matches the code.

**Choices and loose ends**
- Biome 2.6 also formats Markdown, so I excluded `*.md` (and `hq.json`) from it to keep it off the docs.
- I made the registry login and image name Terraform variables, so nothing depends on the registry's `urn` attribute, which the plan flagged as unconfirmed.
- The iOS bundle ID is a placeholder, `com.durhack.kip`.
- The tRPC client doesn't send a user ID yet; the `account` feature should add it.
- `MIN_NIGHTS_FOR_PERCENTAGE = 5` is a provisional number of mine. The plan only says "several nights".

Should I push and open a PR so CI runs?
push and open pr

| Resource | Notes |

derives `<ip>.sslip.io` from instance metadata, logs in to the registry and starts the API, the
worker and Caddy. Outputs: `api_ip`, `api_url`, `registry_urn`.

## First apply
1. Credentials in your shell (from 1Password or the MLH emails, never committed):
   `VULTR_API_KEY`, `MONGODB_ATLAS_PUBLIC_KEY`, `MONGODB_ATLAS_PRIVATE_KEY`.

3. Create the registry first, then push the image to it:
   ```bash
   terraform -chdir=infra init
   terraform -chdir=infra apply -target=vultr_container_registry.kip
   terraform -chdir=infra output registry_urn          # e.g. lhr.vultrcr.com/kip
   docker login <registry host>                        # registry credentials from the Vultr console
   docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t <registry_urn>/kip:latest .
   docker push <registry_urn>/kip:latest
   ```
   Set `image = "<registry_urn>/kip:latest"` and the registry credentials in `terraform.tfvars`.
4. `terraform -chdir=infra apply`. Give cloud-init a few minutes, then open `api_url`.

## Ship a new build
```bash
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t <registry_urn>/kip:latest . && docker push <registry_urn>/kip:latest
ssh root@$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw api_ip) 'cd /opt/kip && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d'
```

```bash
terraform -chdir=infra plan
terraform -chdir=infra apply -replace=vultr_instance.api

name: hq-review
description: Use when asked to review someone else's PR ("review PR 12" or "/hq-review 12"). Checks it against the linked issue and sets review:pass or review:changes.

# hq-review

Review in your own worktree or workspace, never in the author's. Prefer a reviewer from a
different vendor than the author (the PR's `agent:*` label).

1. Check out the PR: `gh pr checkout <PR>`.
2. Find the issue: `gh pr view <PR> --json title,labels,closingIssuesReferences`, then

   - Verdict: pass or changes.
   - Each acceptance criterion: met or not met, with evidence.

7. Post it: `gh pr review <PR> --comment --body-file .context/review-<PR>.md`.
   Use `--comment`: you cannot approve a PR opened from your own account.
8. Label it:
   - pass: `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass --remove-label review:changes`
   - changes: `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:changes --remove-label review:pass`
9. Do not push fixes to the author's branch and do not merge. Tell the human the verdict.
